claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Controlled grain-boundary chemistry is the primary factor governing the proposed enhancement in plastic strain and toughness.
Zr preferentially segregates to WTaTiVZr grain boundaries at operating temperatures.
Ta, Ti, or V may also segregate to WTaTiVZr grain boundaries to a lesser extent than Zr.
Solute segregation increases grain-boundary cohesion in WTaTiVZr.
Increased grain-boundary cohesion retards intergranular crack initiation.
Increased grain-boundary cohesion retards intergranular crack propagation.
Zr segregation facilitates grain-boundary sliding without catastrophic failure.
Zr segregation may permit easier dislocation motion.
Pure tungsten lacks the proposed beneficial solute-segregation mechanism and consequently has a more brittle response.
An as-cast equimolar WTaTiVZr specimen can have a uniform polycrystalline microstructure with minimal secondary-phase precipitation.
The range 1200–1500 K is representative of high-temperature plasma-facing-component service.
Diffusion at approximately 1200–1500 K enables significant Zr segregation in WTaTiVZr.
The segregation mechanism may become kinetically limited at substantially lower temperatures.
At sufficiently high temperatures, phase instability or excessive irradiation damage may invalidate the proposed mechanism.
WTaTiVZr should exhibit higher fracture toughness than pure tungsten under otherwise identical high-temperature test conditions.
WTaTiVZr should exhibit greater ductility and plastic strain than pure tungsten under otherwise identical high-temperature test conditions.
TEM/EDS examination should reveal Zr enrichment at WTaTiVZr grain boundaries.
Controlled atmospheres can mimic irradiation effects relevant to plasma-facing service.

contradictions.description: The comparison changes the entire composition from pure W to five-component WTaTiVZr rather than selectively manipulating grain-boundary Zr segregation. It therefore does not isolate grain-boundary chemistry as the cause despite the claim that composition is the only intended variable.

The conditions propose a controlled atmosphere to mimic irradiation effects, while the boundary invokes excessive irradiation damage; no actual irradiation exposure, dose, or damage rate is included, so irradiation-dependent validity cannot be tested by the stated experiment.
